analysis.title: Americas Pipelines and MLPs: Remain Constructive on Natural Gas Pipelines After Recent Volatility; Focus on Buy-Rated WMB and TRP; DTM Up to Neutral
key_insights: GS stays constructive on natural gas pipelines despite debate over the data center power outlook. The supports are solid 3Q26 earnings updates and possible permitting reform. The group (AM, DTM, ENB, ET, KMI, TRP, WMB) is down 5% over six months versus AMZ down 1%.

Four reasons the group is well positioned: lower-beta exposure to gas demand growth, high contracting with little pre-FID project EBITDA in near-to-medium-term estimates, 3Q26 updates showing more willingness from utilities and hyperscalers to support gas projects, and progress on permit reform in DC.

GS sees natural gas transmission EBITDA CAGRs of 5-10% over 2026-2032 as highly compelling for a sector normally defined by low-single-digit growth. Demand-pull sources (utility-scale power, LNG feedgas) are favored over supply-push.

GS reiterates its August view that data center power demand drives ~10-11 bcf/d of incremental US gas demand by 2030. This rests on the GS Utilities and Power team's forecast of ~108 GW of US data center power demand by 2030 (~69 GW of growth 2025-2030). GS assumes gas fuels ~60% of ~47 GW on-grid growth and 100% of ~22 GW behind-the-meter growth. The estimate is at the low end of industry forecasts of 10-15+ bcf/d.
Pipelines are sized for peak-day loads, so GS expects gas transmission additions to exceed physical demand growth.

Almost all 2026-28 incremental EBITDA growth for the group is already sanctioned, as is a large share of 2029-32 growth. Sanctioned backlogs are ~14-15% of 2026 EV across coverage. Build multiples are ~6x for many projects against run-rate valuations of ~12x.

The US Senate voted to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) permitting bill, and President Trump endorsed it. GS calls permitting reform an under-appreciated catalyst: NEPA exemptions, narrowed state authority under the Clean Water Act, and faster deadlines. GS takes no view on final passage. Project announcements could accelerate as soon as 2H27. Easier permitting could also erode existing pipeline franchises over time.

Post-election risks to pre-FID project execution include state-level approvals for data center projects and permitting timelines for new greenfields. Impacts are later-dated because much of the growth is contracted. State watch list: Ohio and Texas for WMB, the Midwest for TRP, Georgia for KMI (Democrat-controlled PSC and the Southern Company JV), New Mexico for ET.

Valuation framework: 2027E target multiples for gas-weighted names are 12.5-15x. On GS price targets, 2030E EV/EBITDA compresses to 8.0-13.0x, and the gas coverage average compresses two turns from 2027E to 2030E. WMB goes from 15x on 2027E to 11.4x by 2030 on ~41% EBITDA growth 2027-2030E.

WMB (Buy) is the top idea and a high-conviction call. GS expects ~12% EBITDA CAGR 2025-30, with ~11% already supported by post-FID projects, and 1-2 power project announcements by year-end 2026. Price target cut to $82 from $84 on higher non-controlling interests, with the 15x 2027E multiple unchanged.

TRP (Buy) has ~89% of 2032E EBITDA in gas transmission. Drivers are the sanctioned US$1.8b Crossroads project (above the prior US$1.4b expectation), ~C$25b of pre-FID gas and ~C$15b of pre-FID power in origination (power excluded from GS estimates), and a favorable Canada power backdrop. Price target raised to C$102 / US$73 from C$101 / US$71 on 14.75x 2027E EBITDA.

KMI (Buy) has upcoming project announcements as catalysts. Southeast Connector could be upsized to ~3.5 bcf/d from 2.6 bcf/d, and the Permian Link project is anchored by a single hyperscaler. Two-way risks are 2027 guidance next month, possible RNG M&A, and Georgia policy risk. Price target unchanged at $36 on 12.5x 2027E EBITDA.

DTM upgraded to Neutral from Sell, price target raised to $127 from $121 on 13.5x 2027E EBITDA (up from 13x). Reasons: 2030 consensus EBITDA fell 5% in six months (now ~8.5% CAGR 2025-2030 versus GS ~9%), a solid gas opportunity set, and a more balanced risk/reward after the stock fell 16% in six months versus gas-weighted peers down 3%.

GS expects DTM to raise its five-year organic backlog at 4Q26 earnings from ~$3.4b to roughly $4.3-4.8b, about a 35% increase at the midpoint. That is smaller than the 48% step-up at 4Q25 and 77% at 4Q24. The current ~$2.4b sanctioned backlog is ~15% of EV, and could reach ~19-21% if 70% of the larger backlog is sanctioned within 12 months.

ET (Neutral, PT $22 unchanged on 8.75x 2027E) has the highest gas transmission EBITDA CAGR in coverage (10% 2026-2032E), but gas is only ~27% of the business. Recontracting headwinds in NGL and crude leave it the lowest total EBITDA CAGR (2%). It screens cheapest at 8.0x 2030E implied EV/EBITDA, with the least multiple compression (0.8x). 2030 consensus is up ~6% in six months, and GS is ~3% below consensus in 2027-2030.

AM (Neutral, PT $23 from $24 on 10.5x, down from 11x) is a largely pure-play West Virginia exposure with gas transmission at ~8% of 2032E EBITDA. The lower multiple reflects higher risk to Antero Resources' growth amid a softer gas backdrop. Investors need more concrete project announcements before underwriting growth.

ENB (Neutral) has gas pipelines at only ~30% of 2032E EBITDA and ~5% total EBITDA CAGR 2026-2032E. Leverage is 5.1x at 3Q26, above the target range, and the pending Tallgrass (US$2.55b) and Laramie (US$485m) acquisitions are a near-term focus. Price target C$71 / US$50 from C$70 / US$49 on 13x 2027E EBITDA. The December guidance update is the next catalyst.

sector_views.rationale: Contracted, demand-pull growth backlogs, a low-beta link to gas demand, possible permitting reform and falling implied multiples through 2030.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 results showed power-related project backlogs still expanding, with LNG growth and non-data center power opportunities emerging as another demand leg. Examples are KMI's Southeast Connector and Permian Link projects, the latter anchored by a single hyperscaler.

TRP 3Q26 update was strong and included the sanctioned US$1.8b Crossroads project. TRP guided to a 5-7% EBITDA CAGR 2026-31. GS 2027 EBITDA estimate of C$12.39b (GSe) is in line with the midpoint of the C$12.3-12.5b guidance range, and its 2031 estimate of C$15.51b is below TRP's implied 2031 guidance of C$15.92b.
ET 2026 EBITDA estimate of $19.59b (GSe, up 2% from prior) compares with consensus of $19.57b. It reflects stronger marketing margin and gas contributions, offsetting lower crude margin.
ENB 2026 EBITDA estimate of C$20.52b (GSe) is in line with the midpoint of the C$20.2-20.8b guidance range. ENB leverage was 5.1x at 3Q26.
KMI 2027 guidance is due next month and DTM 4Q26 earnings are the next catalyst for its backlog update. ENB gives a guidance update in December.
Consensus 2030 adjusted EBITDA revisions over six months, adjusted for transactions: ET +6%, WMB +5%, TRP +4%, AM +4%, KMI +3%, ENB 0%, DTM -5%.

risk_factors: Post-election risk to pre-FID backlog execution and slower new project announcements if tougher permitting scenarios play out.
Data center power demand uncertainty, including on-grid approvals.
LNG feedgas infrastructure demand may slow by the early 2030s, and renewables penetration could reduce system utilization.
Looser permitting could lower barriers to entry and erode regional pipeline franchises.

tension_points.bull_case: BAAJA would exempt work on existing corridors from NEPA, narrow state authority under the Clean Water Act and speed permitting deadlines. That lowers execution risk and capex, speeds in-service dates, and could lift project announcements from 2H27.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors remain skeptical because comprehensive efforts have failed before. Looser permitting would also lower barriers to entry for new developers and erode the monopoly or oligopoly of existing regional franchises. Post-election state-level approvals remain a concern.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The bill failing to clear the remaining steps: the Senate amendment process, a final Senate floor vote, House passage and the President's signature.

tension_points.theme: data center gas demand and pre-FID backlog
tension_points.bull_case: GS sees ~10-11 bcf/d of incremental gas demand by 2030, at the low end of industry forecasts, and expects power project FIDs before year-end. Sanctioned backlogs are ~14-15% of EV.
tension_points.bear_case: Post-election uncertainty around on-grid approvals and state-level data center project approvals adds risk to pre-FID projects. LNG feedgas demand may slow by the early 2030s.
tension_points.what_invalidates: WMB announcing no power project FIDs by year-end 2026, or permitting scenarios turning draconian after the election.

tension_points.bull_case: The consensus reset (2030 EBITDA down 5%) and the 16% six-month underperformance leave a balanced risk/reward. A backlog update to $4.3-4.8b at 4Q26 could re-anchor sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: Compression leans on pre-FID projects (MIST Phase 2+, Vector 2030, Millennium, NEXUS), so GS stays balanced until they reach FID. Midwest and Northeast permitting is a risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 4Q26 backlog update below the $4.3-4.8b range, or slow conversion of pre-FID projects to FID.
